mainTopic: A woman who discharges a חתיכה: whether the womb can open without blood, tests for blood or bone inside the tissue, and blood that comes out through a tube (שפופרת)
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about a woman who miscarried something she cannot identify. The תנא קמא treats her as a ספק, so her קרבן is not eaten. רבי יהושע says it is eaten, because the womb cannot open without blood. In a second version of the discussion, שמואל limits רבי יהודה's ruling to a חתיכה with an impure blood color. A ברייתא from רב הושעיא disproves this, so רב יהודה explains that the argument is whether the womb can open without blood. The גמרא then lists views on tearing open a חתיכה: סומכוס counts blood inside it, רבי אחא counts even a red inside, and רבי שמעון בן יוחאי needs collected blood. רבי בנימין says a bone inside a white piece makes it a birth. רבי זירא learns from בבשרה that blood coming out through a tube (שפופרת) does not make her טמאה, and he explains why tissue is different. The גמרא suggests the tube question is a dispute between תנאים. אביי rejects that suggestion, saying everyone agrees she is טהורה, and the explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא: she is a ספק יולדת and a ספק זבה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that the woman is a ספק לידה and a ספק זיבה. She brings a קרבן, but it may not be eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: This woman is in doubt: maybe she gave birth, maybe she is a זבה. So she brings a קרבן, but it is not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it began quoting earlier. The תנא קמא rules that this woman is in a state of doubt, so her קרבן is brought but not eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If she gave birth or became a זבה, she must bring a bird קרבן. But maybe she is neither, and then the bird is not a real קרבן. A bird killed by מליקה (pinching the neck) that is not a true קרבן is forbidden to eat, so the כהנים may not eat it.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt whether she has the status of a woman who gave birth
A doubt whether she has the status of a זבה, a woman with an irregular discharge of blood
An offering; here, the bird offering a יולדת or זבה brings
And it is not eaten by the כהנים

phrases.english: this woman is a doubtful case of birth
and a doubtful case of zava;
she brings an offering, but it is not eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי זוֹ סְפֵק לֵידָה סְפֵק זִיבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted earlier on the daf to explain the dispute in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The woman is a ספק יולדת and a ספק זבה. She brings a קרבן, but it is not eaten.

steps.title: רבי יהושע: the offering is eaten, because the womb cannot open without blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע argues that the קרבן is eaten. Opening of the womb always comes with blood, so she is definitely obligated in a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: she brings a קרבן and it is eaten, because the womb cannot open without blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives רבי יהושע's opposing view. He holds the קרבן is eaten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יהושע, there is no real doubt about whether she owes a קרבן. If the womb opened, blood certainly came out, so either way (birth or זיבה) she must bring one. Her קרבן is therefore a true obligation and may be eaten. This is the same disagreement the גמרא uses to explain the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים in the משנה.
steps.whatToRemember: The core question is whether the womb can open without blood. רבי יהושע says it cannot, so blood is assumed even when none was seen.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle is the basis the גמרא uses to explain why רבי יהודה rules a woman impure even when no blood was seen with the חתיכה.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
she brings an offering, and it is eaten,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִפְתִיחַת הַקֶּבֶר בְּלֹא דָּם.
phrases.english: for it is impossible for the womb to open without blood.
phrases.notes: 'The grave' is the גמרא's way of saying the womb.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מְבִיאָה קׇרְבָּן וְנֶאֱכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing opinion within the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קרבן is eaten, because opening of the womb is impossible without blood.

steps.title: Another version: שמואל limits רבי יהודה to pieces with the four impure blood colors
steps.stepSummary: In a different version of the discussion, רב יהודה quotes שמואל: רבי יהודה ruled impure only when the חתיכה has the color of one of the four impure types of blood. Any other color is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some tell it another way. רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: רבי יהודה ruled the woman impure only for a piece that looks like one of the four impure types of blood. If it looks like other types of blood, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version (לישנא אחרינא) of how to understand רבי יהודה in the משנה. שמואל narrows רבי יהודה's ruling of טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this version, רבי יהודה's ruling depends on the look of the piece itself, and only pieces with an impure blood color make her טמאה. A piece with a color that is not an impure blood color leaves her טהורה. This limitation is what the next step will challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same discussion
A piece of tissue discharged from the womb
The four types (colors) of blood that make a woman impure

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new topic. It is a second version (לישנא אחרינא) of how the earlier discussion of רבי יהודה went.

phrases.english: Some say it in another version:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
Rabbi Yehuda ruled her impure

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בַּחֲתִיכָה שֶׁל אַרְבָּעָה מִינֵי דָמִים,
phrases.english: only for a piece with the look of the four types of blood,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל שֶׁל שְׁאָר מִינֵי דָמִים — טְהוֹרָה.
phrases.english: but for one with the look of other types of blood, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחְרִינָא אָמְרִי לַהּ: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a different version of the discussion of רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה rules impure only for a חתיכה with the color of one of the four impure types of blood. Other colors are pure.

steps.title: Challenge from רב הושעיא's ברייתא: רבי יהודה rules impure even for green and white pieces
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא brought by רב הושעיא. It lists red, black, green and white pieces, and רבי יהודה rules impure in every case, even without blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? When רב הושעיא came from נהרדעא, he brought a ברייתא with him: A woman who discharges a piece that is red, black, green or white is impure if blood comes with it, and pure if not. רבי יהודה says: either way, she is impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's limitation using a ברייתא. In that ברייתא, רבי יהודה seems to rule impure for all these colors.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Green and white are not among the impure colors of blood. Yet in the ברייתא, רבי יהודה says 'either way she is impure' about the whole list. This seems to show that רבי יהודה rules impure even for pieces that do not have an impure blood color, against שמואל. The answer to this challenge comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? (a word that opens a challenge)
A woman who discharges or miscarries

phrases.english: Is that so?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא,
phrases.english: But when Rav Hoshaya came from Neharde'a,
he came and brought a baraita with him:
A woman who discharges a piece that is red,
or black, green, or white,
phrases.notes: Green and white are not impure colors of blood, and that is the point of the challenge.

phrases.english: if there is blood with it, she is impure,
and if not, she is pure.
And Rabbi Yehuda says:
either way, she is impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא כִּי אֲתָא רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's limitation from step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that רבי יהודה rules impure only for pieces with one of the four impure blood colors.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא includes green and white pieces, which are not impure blood colors. Still, רבי יהודה rules 'either way, she is impure,' which seems to cover every color in the list.

steps.title: The punchline: רבי יהודה argues even on green and white
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא lists red, black, green and white pieces, and רבי יהודה disagrees about all of them. This contradicts שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ברייתא lists red and black, and also green and white, and רבי יהודה disagrees in all of them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its attack on שמואל. The ברייתא includes green and white pieces, and רבי יהודה still disagrees.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said רבי יהודה rules impure only when the piece has the color of impure blood. Green and white are not impure blood colors. If רבי יהודה rules impure even for them, his reason cannot be the color.

keyTerms.meaning: Red, one of the impure blood colors
Green, not one of the impure blood colors
White, not one of the impure blood colors

phrases.english: It teaches "red and black,"
"green and white,"
phrases.notes: Green and white are not colors of impure blood. That is what makes this list a problem for שמואל.

phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda disagrees!

steps.triggerLanguage: קָתָנֵי אֲדוּמָּה וּשְׁחוֹרָה יְרוּקָּה וּלְבָנָה וּפְלִיג רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge opened in step 4 by stating its punchline.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that רבי יהודה rules impure only when the piece has an impure blood color.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא has רבי יהודה disagreeing even about green and white pieces, which are not impure blood colors.

steps.title: A possible defense: maybe רבי יהודה argues only on red and black
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a way to save שמואל: maybe רבי יהודה disagrees only about the red and black pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: רבי יהודה disagrees only about red and black, but about green and white he does not disagree.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to defend שמואל by reading the ברייתא differently. This defense is set up so the גמרא can knock it down in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, רבי יהודה agrees that green and white pieces are pure. That would fit שמואל's color rule perfectly.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say, which introduces a suggested answer
Black, one of the impure blood colors

phrases.english: And if you would say,
when Rabbi Yehuda disagrees,
it is about red and black,
but about green and white, he does not,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible defense of שמואל against the challenge in step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of רבי יהודה's disagreement within the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה disagrees about every color in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Suggested: רבי יהודה disagrees only about red and black.

steps.title: The defense fails: the green and white case must be there for רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: If רבי יהודה agrees about green and white, there is no reason to list them. The רבנן already call even red and black pure, so green and white are obvious for them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, for whose sake does it list green and white? If you say for the רבנן, that is pointless. They call even red and black pure, so of course green and white are pure! So it must be listed for רבי יהודה, and he disagrees.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the defense. Every case in a ברייתא must teach something, and green and white only teach something if רבי יהודה disagrees about them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the רבנן, green and white teach nothing new, because they call even the harder case of red and black pure. So the only reason to list green and white is to show that רבי יהודה rules impure even there. That brings the challenge against שמואל back in full force.

keyTerms.meaning: For whom does it teach it? Whose opinion does this case come to show?
If we say, which introduces a possibility the גמרא is about to reject
Now, used to open a 'this is obvious' argument
Is it even a question? Meaning it is obvious
Rather, is it not that, which pushes toward the only remaining option

phrases.english: But then, green and white,
for whose sake does it teach it?
If we say for the Rabbis,
now, red and black
the Rabbis declare pure,
do green and white even need to be said?
Rather, is it not for Rabbi Yehuda, and he disagrees!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא יְרוּקָּה וּלְבָנָה מַאן קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the defense proposed in step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that רבי יהודה disagrees only about red and black, and so rejects שמואל's explanation.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: For the Rabbis, the green and white case would teach nothing new, so it must be there to show רבי יהודה's disagreement.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that every case in a ברייתא must teach something, is why שמואל's explanation is dropped and a new one is needed.

steps.title: רב יהודה's new explanation: can the womb open without blood?
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the רבנן and רבי יהודה argue about whether פתיחת הקבר can happen without blood. This is the same issue that other תנאים argue about.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יהודה said: they argue about whether the womb can open without blood, and this is the same argument as one between other תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: Since שמואל's explanation failed, רב יהודה offers a completely different reason for the argument. He also says it matches an earlier argument between תנאים, which the גמרא will quote next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument is no longer about the color of the piece. It is about whether the womb can open without releasing blood. If it cannot, then expelling any piece, of any color, means blood came out, which explains why רבי יהודה rules impure in every case.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up רב יהודה (the אמורא speaking here) with רבי יהודה (the תנא whose opinion is being explained).

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yehuda said:
about whether the womb can open without blood
they disagree,
and it is the same as the argument of these תנאים,

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces שמואל's rejected explanation with a new one.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A new reason for the argument
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שמואל: the argument depends on the color of the piece.
steps.terutzMaskana: The argument is whether the womb can open without blood.
steps.whyThisMatters: This new reason explains why רבי יהודה rules impure no matter what color the piece is.

steps.title: The ברייתא of the תנאים quoted again
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא about a woman who had hard labor for two days and miscarried something unknown on the third. She is in doubt, so she brings a קרבן that is not eaten.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a woman had hard labor for two days, and on the third day she miscarried, but she does not know what she miscarried. She might count as having given birth, or she might be a זבה. She brings a קרבן, but it is not eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא from earlier, now as the source for רב יהודה's comparison. This step sets up the tannaic argument that רב יהודה is linking to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same ברייתא that ended at the start of the amud. In this second version, רב יהודה is the one who links it to the argument between the רבנן and רבי יהודה. The opposing view of רבי יהושע, that the womb never opens without blood, is the other side of that argument.

keyTerms.meaning: In doubt whether she counts as having given birth
In doubt whether she is a זבה
It is not eaten, because the קרבן may not be needed

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל's color explanation was rejected. רב יהודה says the argument is about whether the womb can open without blood, and he links it to the argument in this ברייתא.

phrases.english: as it was taught:
she had hard labor for two days,
phrases.notes: She saw blood on those two days while in labor.

phrases.english: and on the third day she miscarried,
and she does not know what she miscarried,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרֵי זוֹ סְפֵק לֵידָה סְפֵק זִיבָה,
phrases.english: she is in doubt whether she gave birth and in doubt whether she is a zavah,
she brings an offering, but it is not eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא קִשְּׁתָה שְׁנַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source that רב יהודה pointed to in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's claim that the Rabbis and רבי יהודה argue about the same issue as these תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about hard labor followed by an unknown miscarriage, together with רבי יהושע's opposing view

steps.title: רבי יהושע: The womb cannot open without blood
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע disagrees with the first opinion in the ברייתא. He says the woman brings a קרבן that is eaten, because the womb cannot open without blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע says: She brings a קרבן and it is eaten, because the womb cannot open without blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from Step 9. This line gives the second opinion, which completes the proof that תנאים argue about פתיחת הקבר בלא דם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said she is in doubt, so her קרבן is not eaten. רבי יהושע says there is no doubt: if the womb opened, blood definitely came out, so she is either a יולדת or a זבה and owes a real קרבן. This is the same view as רבי יהודה in our משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering that is eaten, meaning a definite קרבן, not one brought out of doubt

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the argument between the רבנן and רבי יהודה in our משנה is an older argument between תנאים, as רב יהודה said in Step 8.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua says:
She brings an offering, and it is eaten,

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאִי אֶפְשָׁר לִפְתִיחַת הַקֶּבֶר בְּלֹא דָּם.
phrases.english: because it is impossible for the womb to open without blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אוֹמֵר: מְבִיאָה קׇרְבָּן וְנֶאֱכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in Step 9 by giving the opposing opinion.
steps.raayaObject: רב יהודה's claim that the רבנן and רבי יהודה argue about whether the womb can open without blood
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of the woman with a hard labor: the first opinion treats it as a doubt, and רבי יהושע says the womb cannot open without blood.

steps.title: סומכוס: Tear open the tissue and check for blood inside
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא: סומכוס, in the name of רבי מאיר, says that if a woman miscarries a piece of tissue, you tear it open. If there is blood inside, she is impure. If not, she is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: A woman who miscarries a piece of tissue: סומכוס says in the name of רבי מאיר, and רבי שמעון בן מנסיא said the same: Tear it open. If there is blood inside it, she is impure. If not, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא with another opinion about the piece of tissue from our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה spoke about blood that comes out together with the tissue. This ברייתא adds a new test: tear the tissue open and look for blood inside it.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who miscarries a piece of tissue

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: A woman who miscarries a piece of tissue,
Sumchos says in the name of Rabbi Meir,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן מְנַסְיָא אוֹמֵר כִּדְבָרָיו:
phrases.english: and Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya would also say like his words:

phrases.aramaic: קוֹרְעָהּ, אִם יֵשׁ דָּם בְּתוֹכָהּ — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: One tears it open. If there is blood inside it, she is impure,
and if not, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַמַּפֶּלֶת חֲתִיכָה, סוֹמְכוֹס אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: another ברייתא about the piece of tissue from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tear open the miscarried tissue. Blood inside means she is impure, and no blood means she is pure.

steps.title: סומכוס agrees with the רבנן but is stricter
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that סומכוס agrees with the רבנן that the womb can open without blood. But he is stricter than them, because even blood found inside the tissue makes her impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like the רבנן, and it goes further than the רבנן. It is like the רבנן, who say the womb can open without blood. It goes further than the רבנן, because they hold that blood with the tissue makes her impure, but blood inside it does not. סומכוס holds that even blood inside it makes her impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא places סומכוס's opinion on the map of our משנה's argument. He is on the side of the רבנן, but stricter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס is not like רבי יהודה, because he says that with no blood she is pure, so the womb can open without blood. He is stricter than the רבנן, because for them only blood that comes out with the tissue counts, while for him blood found inside the tissue also counts.

keyTerms.meaning: With it, meaning blood that came out together with the tissue

steps.confusionAlert: סומכוס is stricter than the רבנן, but that does not make him like רבי יהודה. רבי יהודה says she is impure even with no blood at all. סומכוס still says that with no blood, she is pure.
steps.whatToRemember: There are three levels. The רבנן count only blood that comes out with the tissue. סומכוס also counts blood inside the tissue. רבי יהודה says she is always impure, because the womb cannot open without blood.

phrases.english: It is like the Rabbis, and it goes further than the Rabbis.
It is like the Rabbis, who say:
phrases.notes: "The Rabbis" here are the first opinion in our משנה, who argue with רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: it is possible for the womb to open without blood.
And it goes further than the Rabbis,
because they hold: blood with it, yes, she is impure,
blood inside it, no, she is not impure,
and Sumchos holds: even blood inside it makes her impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּרַבָּנַן, וַעֲדִיפָא מִדְּרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא of סומכוס from Step 11 and compares it to the opinions in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סומכוס agrees with the רבנן that the womb can open without blood, but he is stricter, because blood inside the tissue also makes her impure.

steps.title: רבי אחא: A red inside is enough to make her impure
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: רבי אחא says to tear open the tissue. If its inside looks red, she is impure. If not, she is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: A woman who miscarries a piece of tissue: רבי אחא says: Tear it open. If its inside is reddish, she is impure. If not, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא about the piece of tissue, with an even stricter test.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סומכוס required actual blood inside the tissue. רבי אחא goes one step further: even if there is no actual blood, a red color inside is enough to make her impure.
steps.whatToRemember: This builds a ladder of strictness for the tissue: blood with it (רבנן), blood inside it (סומכוס), and a red color inside it (רבי אחא).

phrases.english: And another baraita teaches: A woman who miscarries a piece of tissue,
Rabbi Acha says: One tears it open,
if its inside looks red, she is impure,
and if not, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ: הַמַּפֶּלֶת חֲתִיכָה, רַבִּי אַחָא אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a parallel ברייתא with a stricter test than סומכוס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the inside of the tissue looks red, she is impure. If not, she is pure.

steps.title: Comparing רבי אחא to סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי אחא follows the same approach as סומכוס but goes even further.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like סומכוס, and it goes further than סומכוס.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא places רבי אחא's opinion from the last step next to סומכוס's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both say to tear the tissue open and look inside. סומכוס needs actual blood inside, but רבי אחא makes her impure even if the inside only looks red. That makes רבי אחא stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: goes further than / is more extreme than
a piece of tissue with no clear shape

phrases.english: This is like סומכוס,
phrases.notes: This refers to רבי אחא's ruling from the last step: tear it open, and if the inside is red, she is impure.

phrases.english: and it goes further than סומכוס.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּסוֹמְכוֹס, וַעֲדִיפָא מִסּוֹמְכוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the גמרא's own assessment of the ברייתא of רבי אחא quoted in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אחא agrees with סומכוס that the inside of the tissue matters, but he is stricter, because redness alone is enough.

steps.title: רבי בנימין: a bone inside makes it a birth
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא: רבי בנימין says to tear open the tissue, and if there is a bone inside, the mother has the impurity of a woman who gave birth.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another ברייתא teaches: if a woman miscarries a piece of tissue, רבי בנימין says you tear it open. If it has a bone in it, the mother is impure as after a birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more ברייתא about torn-open tissue. This one checks for a bone, not for blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier opinions were asking whether there is blood, which would mean ordinary נדה impurity. רבי בנימין asks something different: is this a baby? A bone shows it was a fetus, so she gets טומאת לידה.

keyTerms.meaning: impure with the impurity of a woman who gave birth

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with the blood opinions. A bone does not just make her impure as a נדה. It means she had a birth, which carries different laws.

phrases.english: And it is taught in another ברייתא:
A woman who miscarries a piece of tissue,
Rabbi Binyamin says: one tears it open.
If it has a bone in it,
its mother is impure as one who gave birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא אִידַּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third ברייתא about tearing open tissue, now looking for a bone instead of blood.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tissue with a bone inside counts as a fetus, so the mother is טמאה לידה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: only a white piece
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא limits רבי בנימין's ruling to a white piece of tissue.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: and this is talking about a white piece of tissue.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא adds a condition to רבי בנימין's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not every tissue with a bone is treated as a birth. According to רב חסדא, the bone rule applies when the tissue is white.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
And this is with a white piece of tissue.
phrases.notes: He is explaining which case רבי בנימין's bone rule is talking about.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וּבַחֲתִיכָה לְבָנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the case of רבי בנימין's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bone rule applies to a white piece of tissue.

steps.title: A ברייתא from חדייב supports רב חסדא
steps.stepSummary: Scholars from חדייב brought a ברייתא that says outright "a white piece," which matches רב חסדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, when a pair of scholars came from חדייב, they brought a ברייתא with them: a woman who miscarries a white piece of tissue, you tear it open, and if it has a bone, the mother is impure as after a birth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that רב חסדא's condition actually appears in a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from חדייב is the same as רבי בנימין's, but it adds the word "white." This shows that רב חסדא was not making up a new limit. He was reporting what this ברייתא says.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא זוּגָא דְּמִן חַדְיָיב,
phrases.english: And likewise, when a pair came from Chadyav,
phrases.notes: חדייב is a place name. The "pair" is two Torah scholars from there.

phrases.english: they came and brought a ברייתא with them:
A woman who miscarries a white piece of tissue,
one tears it open.
If it has a bone in it,
its mother is impure as one who gave birth.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן כִּי אֲתָא זוּגָא דְּמִן חַדְיָיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב חסדא's limit from step 16.
steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's statement that the bone rule is about a white piece of tissue.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא brought by two scholars from חדייב that says "a white piece."
steps.whatToRemember: A bone inside a white piece of tissue makes it a birth (טומאת לידה). רב חסדא said so, and the ברייתא from חדייב says the same thing.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: only collected blood makes her impure
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: tear the tissue open, and she is impure only if there is collected blood inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: if a woman miscarries a piece of tissue, you tear it open. If it has collected blood in it, she is impure. If not, she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more opinion about tearing the tissue open and checking for blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a little blood or a red color is not enough. There must be a real amount of collected blood (דם אגור) inside before she becomes impure.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
A woman who miscarries a piece of tissue: one tears it open.

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ דָּם אָגוּר — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: If it has collected blood in it, she is impure,
and if not, she is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the blood-inside-the-tissue question from steps 11-14 after the bone side-topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only collected blood inside the tissue makes her impure.

steps.title: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי is the most lenient
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says רבי שמעון בן יוחאי follows סומכוס's approach but is more lenient than all the others.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like סומכוס, and it is more lenient than all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא places רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's opinion on the scale next to the others, just as it did with רבי אחא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like סומכוס, he says blood inside the tissue counts. But סומכוס is satisfied with any blood, and רבי אחא even with redness. רבי שמעון בן יוחאי needs collected blood, so he is the most lenient.
steps.whatToRemember: Strictest to most lenient on blood inside the tissue: רבי אחא (red color is enough), then סומכוס (any blood), then רבי שמעון בן יוחאי (only collected blood).

phrases.english: This is like סומכוס,
and it is more lenient than all of them.
phrases.notes: "All of them" means סומכוס and רבי אחא.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּסוֹמְכוֹס, וְקִילָּא מִכּוּלְּהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the גמרא's assessment of the opinion in step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי agrees with סומכוס in principle but is the most lenient of all.

steps.title: Is blood seen through a tube impure?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks רבי זירא whether a woman who sees blood through a tube is impure, and gives two ways to read the word "בבשרה."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked רבי זירא: if a woman sees blood through a tube, what is the law? The Torah says "in her flesh," so maybe that excludes a tube. Or maybe "in her flesh" is needed for a different lesson: that she becomes impure from blood inside her body just as from blood that comes outside.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבי ירמיה asks a question and lays out both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Side one: "בבשרה" means the blood must touch her flesh, so blood that passes through a tube does not count. Side two: "בבשרה" is used up teaching that blood inside the body already makes her impure, so it cannot also exclude a tube.

keyTerms.meaning: the Merciful One, meaning the Torah
it is needed (for a different lesson)

steps.confusionAlert: The second side does not say the tube is impure. It only says "בבשרה" is busy with another lesson, so this word cannot be used to exclude the tube.

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked Rabbi Zeira:
A woman who sees blood through a tube, what is the law?
phrases.notes: She put a tube inside her body, and the blood came out through it without touching her flesh.

phrases.english: The Torah said "in her flesh,"
and not through a tube?
Or perhaps this "in her flesh"
is needed
to teach that she becomes impure from blood inside, just as from blood outside?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה מֵרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the tissue discussion ends.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether blood that passes through a tube, without touching her flesh, makes a woman impure, depending on what "בבשרה" comes to teach.

steps.title: The word 'in her flesh' teaches two things
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that blood through a tube does not make her טמאה. The extra word בבשרה ('her flesh' instead of 'the flesh') teaches both rules.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The Torah said 'in her flesh,' and not through a tube. If 'in her flesh' were only needed to teach that she becomes impure from blood inside just like outside, the verse should have said 'in the flesh.' Why say 'in her flesh'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers רבי ירמיה's question from step 20. A woman who sees blood through a tube is טהורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בבשרה could have been needed for only one rule: blood still inside her body makes her טמאה. But the Torah could have said בבשר, 'the flesh,' for that. The added 'her' teaches a second rule: the blood must touch her own flesh, so blood passing through a tube does not count.

keyTerms.meaning: "In her flesh" (ויקרא 15:19). The word the whole discussion is built on.
Inside just like outside. Blood still inside her body makes her טמאה like blood that came out.
Learn two things from it. One word teaches two rules.

steps.whatToRemember: בבשרה teaches two rules: (1) blood inside her body makes her טמאה, and (2) blood that comes out through a tube does not.

phrases.english: He said to him: The Merciful One said "in her flesh"
phrases.notes: רבי זירא is answering רבי ירמיה. The פסוק is ויקרא 15:19.

phrases.english: and not through a tube.
For if "in her flesh" were needed only
to teach that she becomes impure from inside just as from outside,
if so, let the verse say "in the flesh."
Why does it say "in her flesh"?
Learn two things from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: ״בִּבְשָׂרָהּ״ אֲמַר רַחֲמָנָא וְלֹא בִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי ירמיה's question from step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Blood through a tube does not make her טמאה. The added word 'her' in בבשרה excludes it.

steps.title: Challenge from the tissue ruling of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רבי שמעון בן יוחאי said blood inside a piece of tissue makes her טמאה. So why should blood inside a tube be any different?
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יוחנן say in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: A woman who discharges a piece of tissue tears it open. If there is collected blood in it, she is impure, and if not, she is pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי זירא's answer. It brings back the ruling from step 18, where blood that did not touch her flesh (it was inside tissue) still makes her טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the tissue case the blood is wrapped inside the tissue and never touches her body directly. Yet רבי שמעון בן יוחאי says she is טמאה. A tube seems like the same thing, so it looks like the word בבשרה should not exclude a tube.

keyTerms.meaning: One tears it open to check inside
Collected blood, a gathering of blood inside the tissue

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same ruling quoted in step 18. Here the גמרא repeats it for a new purpose: to attack רבי זירא's tube rule.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say
in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
A woman who discharges a piece of tissue: one tears it open.

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בָּהּ דָּם אָגוּר — טְמֵאָה,
phrases.english: If it has collected blood in it, she is impure,
and if not, she is pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי זירא's rule that blood through a tube is טהור
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Blood inside tissue also does not touch her flesh, yet it makes her טמאה. So a tube should make her טמאה too.

steps.title: Tissue is normal, a tube is not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a woman normally sees blood inside tissue, but she does not normally see blood through a tube.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare? There, it is normal for a woman to see blood in a piece of tissue. Here, it is not normal for a woman to see blood through a tube.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the challenge by showing that the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tissue with blood is a natural way a woman's body releases blood, so it still counts as בבשרה. A tube is something unusual and from outside her body, so the Torah's word 'her flesh' leaves it out.

keyTerms.meaning: "How can you compare?" It rejects a comparison.
The normal way of a woman, what usually happens

steps.whyThisMatters: The line is drawn by what is normal: a natural way for blood to come out counts, and an unnatural one does not.

phrases.english: How can you compare?
There, it is the normal way of a woman
phrases.notes: "There" means the tissue case. "Here" in the next line means the tube.

phrases.english: to see blood in a piece of tissue;
here, it is not the normal way of a woman
to see blood through a tube.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Tissue and a tube are the same, since in both the blood does not touch her flesh
steps.terutzMaskana: Tissue is a normal way for blood to come out, so it counts. A tube is not normal, so it does not count.

steps.title: Is the tube question a dispute among תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the tube question may depend on a dispute among תנאים. It brings a ברייתא about tissue: the first opinion says she is טמאה only if blood comes out with the tissue, and רבי אליעזר learns from בבשרה to exclude a שפיר and a חתיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say the tube case is a dispute among תנאים? As it was taught: A woman who discharges a piece of tissue, even if it is full of blood, is impure if there is blood with it, and if not, she is pure. רבי אליעזר says: 'In her flesh,' and not in a sac and not in a piece of tissue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new suggestion: perhaps the tube question is a disagreement between תנאים. It brings a ברייתא to show it, and the next lines will work out where the two opinions differ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion in the ברייתא says blood inside the tissue alone does not make her טמאה. Only blood that comes out with it does. רבי אליעזר uses the word בבשרה to exclude blood inside a sac or tissue. The גמרא is setting up the question of whether these two views also disagree about a tube.

keyTerms.meaning: "Shall we say it is a dispute of תנאים?" A suggestion that will be tested.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up this ברייתא with רבי שמעון בן יוחאי's ruling. He said collected blood inside the tissue makes her טמאה. The first opinion here says blood inside the tissue alone does not.

phrases.english: Shall we say the tube case is a dispute of תנאים?
As it was taught: A woman who discharges a piece of tissue,
even though it is full of blood,
if there is blood with it, she is impure,
and if not, she is pure.
Rabbi Eliezer says: "In her flesh"
and not in a sac and not in a piece of tissue.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא שְׁפוֹפֶרֶת תַּנָּאֵי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending the tube rule, the גמרא asks whether the rule itself is disputed by תנאים
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the tube question depends on the disagreement between the first opinion and רבי אליעזר in this ברייתא

steps.title: Isn't רבי אליעזר saying the same as the first opinion?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops in the middle of the ברייתא and points out that רבי אליעזר's view sounds identical to the תנא קמא's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר? That is the same as the תנא קמא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses its reading of the ברייתא to raise a problem. רבי אליעזר seems to be saying exactly what the first opinion already said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא said the woman is טמאה only if blood comes out together with the tissue, so blood inside the tissue does not count. רבי אליעזר learns from בבשרה that a שפיר or a חתיכה does not make her טמאה. That is the same ruling, so why is it written as a separate opinion?

keyTerms.meaning: That is the same as..., used to say two opinions are identical
The first, unnamed opinion in a משנה or ברייתא

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer?
That is the same as the first Tanna!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר הַיְינוּ תַּנָּא קַמָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Interrupts the ברייתא quoted in step 24 to question how it is built.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the ברייתא is structured, with רבי אליעזר shown as a separate opinion
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opinions that say the same thing should not be presented as two separate opinions.

steps.title: Fixing the wording: the first part is רבי אליעזר's reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the reading: 'as רבי אליעזר says,' so the first part of the ברייתא is רבי אליעזר's own opinion and its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: 'for רבי אליעזר says: "in her flesh" — and not in a gestational sac and not in a piece of tissue.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by changing one word in the ברייתא. רבי אליעזר is not a second opinion. He is the one who gives the reason for the first opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of 'רבי אליעזר says,' read 'for רבי אליעזר says.' Now the opening ruling and the פסוק בבשרה are one opinion, and the only real argument is with חכמים, who come next. So the problem from step 25 goes away.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead: the גמרא changes the reading of the text
A piece of tissue that comes out of the woman

phrases.english: Say: for Rabbi Eliezer says, "in her flesh"
phrases.notes: The גמרא changes one word to 'for,' so now רבי אליעזר is giving the reason for the first ruling, not adding a new opinion.

phrases.english: and not in a gestational sac and not in a piece of tissue.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא שֶׁרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי אליעזר is a second opinion that repeats the תנא קמא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The opening ruling is רבי אליעזר's, and בבשרה is his source for it.

steps.title: חכמים: it is דם חתיכה, not דם נדה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues with the view of חכמים: blood inside the tissue is דם חתיכה, not דם נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים say: This is not דם נדה, but blood of the piece of tissue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to reading the ברייתא and quotes the opinion of חכמים. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים also say the woman is טהורה, but they give a different reason. For them, this blood simply is not menstrual blood. It belongs to the tissue.

keyTerms.meaning: Menstrual blood, which makes a woman טמאה
Blood that belongs to the piece of tissue itself

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
This is not niddah blood
but blood of the piece of tissue.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים אֵין זֶה דַּם נִדָּה אֶלָּא דַּם חֲתִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא after fixing its wording.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood found in a piece of tissue is tissue blood, not נדה blood, so she is טהורה.

steps.title: The first opinion also says she is pure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the תנא קמא also says she is טהורה, so what are they arguing about?
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא also declares her pure!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא again. Both the תנא קמא and חכמים say the woman is טהורה, so where is the argument?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An argument needs a case where the two sides rule differently. Here both seem to say טהורה for blood in tissue, so the difference is not clear yet.

phrases.english: The first Tanna also declares her pure!

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קַמָּא נָמֵי טַהוֹרֵי מְטַהֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares חכמים in step 27 with the תנא קמא as fixed in step 26.
steps.kashyaTarget: The argument between the תנא קמא and חכמים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If both rule טהורה, there is no case where they disagree.

steps.title: They argue about cracked tissue
steps.stepSummary: The difference between them is a cracked piece of tissue (פלי פלויי).
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the difference between them is a cracked piece of tissue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers in short: they disagree when the tissue is cracked. The next steps explain each side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the tissue has cracks, the blood inside can touch the woman's body. That is the case where the two opinions give different rulings.

phrases.english: Rather, a case where it is cracked
is the difference between them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּפַלַּי פַּלּוֹיֵי אִיכָּא בֵינַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 by finding the case where they disagree.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both always rule טהורה, so there is no argument.

steps.title: The first opinion: smooth tissue is pure, cracked tissue is impure, and a tube is like smooth tissue
steps.stepSummary: For the תנא קמא, blood inside tissue or a tube is טהור only when it is smooth. If the tissue is cracked, the blood touches her flesh, so she is טמאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא קמא holds: "In her flesh" — and not in a gestational sac and not in a piece of tissue, and the same is true of a tube. But this applies only where it is smooth. If it is cracked, she is impure. Why? We read "in her flesh" about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the תנא קמא's view in detail. He also says she is טהורה with a tube, just as with smooth tissue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the תנא קמא, everything depends on whether the blood touches her flesh. Smooth tissue or a tube blocks that contact, so she stays טהורה. Cracked tissue lets the blood touch her, so בבשרה applies and she is טמאה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the same law applies to...
We can read the פסוק about it; it fits the word

phrases.english: The first Tanna holds: "in her flesh"
and not in a gestational sac and not in a piece of tissue,
and the same is true of a tube.
But this applies only where it is smooth,
but if it is cracked, she is impure.
What is the reason?
We read "in her flesh" about it.
phrases.notes: Through the cracks the blood actually touches her body, so it counts as blood 'in her flesh.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא קַמָּא סָבַר בִּבְשָׂרָהּ וְלֹא בַּשָּׁפִיר וְלֹא בַּחֲתִיכָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fills in the תנא קמא's side of the difference named in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining one side of the argument
steps.terutzMaskana: For the תנא קמא, smooth tissue and a tube are טהור, but cracked tissue is טמא because the blood touches her flesh.

steps.title: חכמים: even cracked tissue is pure, because it is דם חתיכה
steps.stepSummary: חכמים say that even when the tissue is cracked, she is טהורה, because the blood is דם חתיכה, not דם נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And חכמים come to say: Even though it is cracked, this is not דם נדה but blood of the tissue.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the side of חכמים. They say she is טהורה even in the cracked case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חכמים, it does not matter whether the blood touched her. What matters is what kind of blood it is, and tissue blood was never נדה blood.

keyTerms.meaning: And they come to say: this is the new point they are making

phrases.english: And the Sages come to say:
even though it is cracked,
this is not niddah blood
but blood of the tissue.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָתוּ רַבָּנַן לְמֵימַר אַף עַל גַּב דְּפַלַּי פַּלּוֹיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side of the difference named in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explaining the second side of the argument
steps.terutzMaskana: For חכמים, cracked tissue is still טהור because it is tissue blood.

steps.title: So for חכמים, דם נדה is impure even through a tube
steps.stepSummary: From the reason of חכמים we learn that real נדה blood makes her טמאה even through a tube. So the tube question is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that דם נדה is certainly impure, and even through a tube!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא draws a conclusion from the reason חכמים gave. This finishes the suggestion from step 24 that the tube question depends on a dispute between תנאים, and the next step rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חכמים say she is טהורה only because it is tissue blood, not because something blocked the blood from touching her. So real נדה blood would make her טמאה even inside a tube. That is the opposite of the תנא קמא, who said a tube is like smooth tissue.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies, an inference from what was just said

steps.whatToRemember: At this point the suggestion is that the tube (שפופרת) question is a dispute between תנאים. The תנא קמא, following בבשרה, says she is טהורה because the blood did not touch her flesh. חכמים seem to care only about whether it is נדה blood, so real נדה blood through a tube would make her טמאה. In the very next step אביי rejects this reading.
steps.confusionAlert: חכמים never mention a tube. Their view on tubes is learned only from the reason they gave for cracked tissue.
steps.whyThisMatters: If this suggestion stood, רבי זירא's ruling in step 21 (tube blood is טהור) would match only the תנא קמא and not חכמים. That is why אביי steps in next to show that everyone agrees about the tube.

phrases.english: This implies that niddah blood is certainly impure,
and even through a tube as well!

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא דַּם נִדָּה וַדַּאי טָמֵא וַאֲפִילּוּ בִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the tube ruling out of the reason חכמים gave in step 31.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The suggestion from step 24 is completed: the תנא קמא would say tube blood is טהור, and חכמים would say real נדה blood is טמא even through a tube. אביי rejects this in step 33.

steps.title: Everyone agrees that with a tube she is pure
steps.stepSummary: אביי rejects the conclusion that the tube case is a מחלוקת תנאים. He says that with a tube (שפופרת), all opinions agree she is טהורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: In the case of a tube, everyone agrees that she is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי pushes back on the last step, which said the tube question is a dispute between תנאים. He says no one argues about the tube: she is טהורה according to everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 32 had read the reasoning of חכמים to mean that real נדה blood makes her טמאה even through a tube. אביי rejects that reading and says a tube always keeps her טהורה, because the blood never touches her flesh. That means the argument between the תנא קמא and חכמים must be about something else, and the גמרא will explain that next.

keyTerms.meaning: A tube; here, a tube inserted so the blood passes through it without touching her body
Pure, meaning she does not become a נדה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think אביי is arguing with the תנאים. He is arguing with the גמרא's last conclusion about what the תנאים were arguing over.
steps.whyThisMatters: This moves the tube case out of the dispute. Everyone agrees on the tube, so the sugya now has to find the real point the תנאים argue about.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
In the case of a tube,
everyone agrees
that she is pure,

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בִּשְׁפוֹפֶרֶת כּוּלֵּי עָלְמָא לָא פְּלִיגִי דִּטְהוֹרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects Step 32's conclusion that the tube case is a dispute between תנאים
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the תנאים disagree about blood that comes out through a tube
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The tube case is not in dispute. All opinions agree she is טהורה, so the argument between the תנא קמא and חכמים must be about something else.
